text:
devon: FYI getting noisy alerts from the capacity monitor — GPU node counts skewed heavily into us-west2-a after last night's Helm rollout. pods with nodeSelector=gpu keep Pending in us-west2-b :eyes:
kevin: link to the alert? can you paste the failing pod events?
maria: saw this too, some node-pools didn't scale up. looks like the autoscaler hit a validation error when creating spot instances in b zone.
devon: pasted events:
```
NAME                 STATUS    REASON             AGE
inference-0-abcde    Pending   \"0/10 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match node selector, 7 Insufficient gpu.\"
```
aj: that message suggests a nodeSelector/label mismatch — did the Helm values change the label key from hardware=gpu to accelerator=gpu?
tina: checking the helm values history now (helm diff showed a small tweak to nodeSelectors in the canary):
```yaml
nodeSelector:
  accelerator: nvidia-tesla-v100
# previously:
# hardware: gpu
```
kevin: ahhh. GitOps vs terraform drift — nodepool labels managed by terraform (gke_nodepool labels) and Helm overwrote expectations in chart. GitOps applied, canary finished, but nodepool resource never updated. autoscaler didn't find matching capacity in us-west2-b and fell back to on-demand in a, causing cost spike.
sre-bot: [incident] capacity-imbalance-us-west2 detected. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/capacity-imbalance (step 2 suggests label reconciliation)
maria: cost note: we already saw a 9% daily GPU spend bump from the fallback. recommend fast reconciliation to avoid further spend & pod disruption.
devon: proposed remediation: 1) add temporary toleration/label on Deployment so pods can land on existing pool in b, 2) fix terraform to set nodepool label correctly and roll nodepool, 3) adjust autoscaler/spot policy so it doesn't fail validation.
aj: quick patch command to allow scheduling while we fix infra (use carefully):
```bash
kubectl patch deploy inference -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"hardware":"gpu"}}}}}'
```
tina: sounds ok for a short window. I'll open a PR to terraform to align the nodepool label key -> apply after approvals.
kevin: plan to apply terraform during low traffic window in 30m, canary deploy the nodepool label change to staging first. I'll also add a preflight Gate in GitOps to diff nodeSelector keys against terraform-managed labels to catch this next time.
maria: also propose a quick lint in our Helm chart CI that fails if nodeSelector key != terraform output for that cluster. saves us from manual diff.
sre-bot: action items recorded: [devon] temporary deployment patch, [tina] terraform PR, [kevin] schedule apply + gate, [maria] helm CI lint.
devon: ok patch applied and pods started scheduling in b. cpu/gpu metrics look stable. keeping watch for any eviction loops. :thumbsup:
kevin: after terraform apply we'll coordinate a controlled drain & rolling recreate so pods pick up the corrected node labels. tracking in #incidents for postmortem.
maria: thanks all — add cost numbers to the postmortem so we can quantify the impact and justify the Helm CI change.
aj: note for followup: consider adding a GitOps preflight that runs `helm get values` and `terraform output node_labels` and diffs them as part of PR status. avoids chart-vs-infra drift.
devon: agreed. closing this thread, will update incidents with final numbers later.
